subject: Trial deliverables & prompt collection — next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@skywardhealth.com>, Priyanka Shah <pri.shah@skywardhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Trial deliverables & prompt collection — next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to align on the scope for the 4-week trial. Below is a concise recap and the asks we agreed on so we can get ingestion and the evaluation run scheduled.

Summary of what we want to validate during the trial
- Functional success: model-generated responses meet your acceptance criteria (see metrics below) on your internal prompt set.
- Latency/throughput: p95 generation latency under 350ms on our dedicated pool for your typical prompt length.
- Safety/compliance: no leakage of PHI/PII in outputs for redacted inputs.

Deliverables we need from Skyward Health (what to send)
1) Sample prompt bundle (initial): 150 representative prompts (CSV) with columns: prompt_id, user_text, context_snippet (optional), expected_response_example, category/tag, and any labels (gold). Redact any PHI before sending.
2) Full prompt set (full trial): up to 3,000 prompts/logs in the same schema or as NDJSON if preferred.
3) Priority evaluation subset: 200 prompts you want us to prioritize for human review.
4) Any domain-specific scoring rubrics or automated tests you use (e.g., allowlists/denylists, canonical answers).

Format & transfer options
- Preferred: S3 bucket access (AWS) or a shared Google Drive folder. If S3, provide a read-only ARN or temporary role.
- Template attached: sample_prompt_template.csv (small stub with expected columns).

Timeline (proposed)
- Initial sample delivered: within 5 business days (target by 2026-11-08).
- Full dataset delivered: within 3 weeks (target by 2026-11-22).
- Redwood evaluation run: complete within 5 business days after receipt of the full dataset; we will share an evaluation report and a short demo.

Success criteria (high level)
- Automated relevance/human score: >= 4.0 / 5.0 average on the priority subset.
- Regression tolerance: no more than 8% drop versus your baseline on key examples.
- Latency: p95 < 350ms (on our dedicated config).
- Critical safety: zero incidents of PHI leakage on sampled redacted logs.

Ownership & contacts
- Skyward lead (data delivery & security): Alex Turner (alex.turner@skywardhealth.com)
- Redwood trial lead & eval owner: Sean Gallagher (sean.gallagher@redwood.ai)
- Ops escalation / billing: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.ai)

Next steps
- Alex: confirm delivery mechanism and whether Skyward will use S3 or Drive.
- Alex: upload the initial sample (150 prompts) and reply here with a link.
- Redwood: prepare ingestion job and an initial evaluation plan on receipt.

Appended: mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf (attached) — milestone dates, roles, and acceptance gates.

Thanks — Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0187

Date: 2026-11-02T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial deliverables & prompt collection — next steps

Thanks Sean — appreciate the clear recap. Quick confirmations from our side:

- We will deliver the initial 150-sample bundle by EOD 2026-11-06. Team will strip direct PHI before export.
- We prefer S3 for the full transfer. We'll create a dedicated prefix and share a temporary read-only role.
- Priority subset: we'll flag 200 prompts and include a short rubric for human scoring (accuracy / helpfulness / hallucination severity).

S3 path (will create and grant access once you confirm the IAM pattern you prefer): s3://skyward-trials/skyward-redwood/prompts/202611
Drive link for initial sample (temporary): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1SamplePromptsDownload

Attaching: (we uploaded the initial CSV to Drive; link above). Our security contact is Priyanka Shah (cc'd) — she will handle the questionnaire and can coordinate with your security team.

One open Q: for expected_response_example, is it OK to include short free-text examples (1-2 sentences) or do you want canonical structured labels? We can include both columns if helpful.

Thanks,
Alex

alex.turner@skywardhealth.com | (650) 555-4201
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@skywardhealth.com>, Priyanka Shah <pri.shah@skywardhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial deliverables & prompt collection — next steps

Perfect — thanks Alex. A few clarifications and a lightweight acceptance checklist so we don't have gaps during the eval:

1) expected_response_example: please include both a short free-text example and an optional canonical label column when available. That helps both automated and human scoring.

2) Redaction guidance: if any prompts contain PHI we only need a redacted placeholder (e.g., [PATIENT_NAME]) plus an internal mapping file you keep offline. Do not send raw PHI.

3) IAM pattern: send us a role ARN in this format: arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT-ID:role/skyward-redwood-trial-readonly. We will confirm minimal permissions required. If easier, you can generate pre-signed S3 URLs for the initial sample.

4) Evaluation metrics (detailed) — what we'll report in the trial summary:
- Human eval: average helpfulness and relevance (1-5), target >= 4.0 on priority subset.
- Automated: BLEU/ROUGE not ideal for your domain; we'll run embedding-similarity and a custom rubric scoring.
- Safety checks: automated PII/PHI detectors + manual spot checks on 100 examples; flag any output that returns redacted tokens.
- Performance: p95 generation latency measured on your median prompt length; target < 350ms.

5) Ownership & communication cadence:
- Weekly sync (30 min) while trial is running — proposed Thursday mornings.
- Any urgent issues: ping marissa.cole@redwood.ai for ops/billing questions, and vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai for infra/throughput tuning.

6) Acceptance gates for trial success (for post-trial decision):
- >= 4.0 human score on prioritized subset AND no safety breaches on spot checks; AND acceptable latency (< 350ms) OR a clear mitigation plan with short timeline.

If that all sounds good I can kick off the ingestion job as soon as we have S3 access or you drop the Drive link.

Thanks — looking forward to the sample.

Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
